ordered_diagnoses: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) of the bile duct

facts.raw_span: no significant past medical history
obstructive jaundice
fever to 38.5 °C
mucocutaneous jaundice, dark urine, and pale stools
no abdominal tenderness, hepatomegaly, or palpable mass
moderate hepatocellular enzyme elevations and cholestasis
Hydatid serology and serum carcinoembryonic antigen and carbohydrate antigen levels were negative
cystic lesion in segment I with parietal and septal enhancement and rupture into the biliary convergence

multiloculated lesion that was hypointense on T1, hyperintense on T2, communicating with the biliary bifurcation, with dilatation of intrahepatic ducts (predominantly left) and of the common bile duct containing heterogeneous signal material
mucinous fluid and membranes were extracted
the liver appeared micronodular
dilatation of intrahepatic ducts (predominantly left) and of the common bile duct
